body: On October 14 the S&P 500 closed 7,718.94, down 1.11%: the worst daily decline since July 29 (-1.52%), with no worse day from July 30 to October 13 (yfinance history, matches AP). The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.88% (worst since July 23), the semiconductor index (SOX) -4.30%, the Russell 2000 -1.93%; VIX closed 16.87 (+10.5%, vendor). AP cites hotter September CPI (3.7% y/y vs 3.6% expected), the 10-year Treasury briefly above 5.32%, and CME odds of another hike at the October 28 FOMC rising to about 35% from 22% (BOND's own futures proxy was about 36%, SIG-W-20261014-017). The new content is AI-infrastructure CREDIT: CoreWeave's $1.25B unsecured notes due 2032 traded near 15% yield intraday and closed about 14.5%, versus 9.625% at issue in June, a distressed-style level (Investing.com relaying Bloomberg; not verified on TRACE). CoreWeave stock closed $65.78, -15.46% (worst day since February per AP; -20.7% vs September 14). A CEO memo seen by Bloomberg, which a spokeswoman confirmed as authentic, says the market 'misunderstands and acts irrationally', that backlog is 'large enough to more than support its debt obligations', and that rivals' weak or delayed IPOs and debt deals are 'bleeding into the narrative'. Same-day AI-infrastructure peers: Oracle -8.83%, Dell -11.27%, Nebius -10.08%, Super Micro -8.42%, Marvell -8.73%, AMD -5.73%, Nvidia about -3.2%. Caveats that travel: one day; the index move is moderate (not a safety-net level); the bond yield is a relayed quote; a CEO statement about backlog coverage is the issuer's own claim. The $800B 'market cap erased' figure in circulation is a rounded-up number (helper's estimate about $0.74-0.78T on a 1.11% move).

title: Bank of America closed -4.8% (the -8.7% was the intraday low); Q3 missed even excluding the $1.2B charge; peers mixed
confidence_language: confirmed at SEC filing and vendor tape
dispatch_note: Will bookmark (BullTheory 'BAC crashes over -8%... down >22% in a month') verified by a RULE 9 helper: CORRECTED-FRAMING. The $1.2B fine is already routed (SIG-W-20261013-015, SIG-W-20261014-004); this adds the market reaction and the adjusted miss. RED on info per the CORRECTED-FRAMING rule.
body: Correcting a widely shared post: BAC did not close down 8%. October 14 (yfinance): open $49.83 (-7.65%), low $49.26 (-8.71%), close $51.39 (-4.76%) vs the $53.96 prior close, about 118M shares; AP also reports -4.8%. The '>22% in a month' figure only holds measuring the September 11 intraday high to the October 14 intraday low; close to close it is -13.6% (vs September 14) to -18.0% (vs September 11). From the 8-K: Q3 net income $6.933B vs $8.332B (-16.8% on the restated year-ago basis), GAAP diluted EPS $0.91, including a $1.2B non-deductible settlement charge (about $0.17 per share) for the OCC/FinCEN penalties. Excluding the charge, EPS $1.08 vs consensus about $1.10 and revenue $29.958B (+3% y/y) vs estimates about $30.6B (secondary), so the quarter missed even without the fine. ROE 9.14% vs 12.09% in Q2. Credit lines improved (net charge-offs $1.349B, 0.44% vs 0.47%). The move was BAC-specific: JPM +1.16%, WFC +0.20%, C -1.81%, MS -2.75%, KBE -0.70%, KRE -0.75%. Caveat: consensus figures are secondary sources; vendor tape is single-source.

title: AI-capex datapoints: TrendForce lifts 9-CSP capex to $957B (2026) and >$1.5T (2027), mostly price-driven; AMD 2030 CPU TAM >$200B; Micron down 16% in five sessions; OpenAI's compute chief leaving
origin: TrendForce OCP coverage October 13 (AMD keynote October 12 PT)
Musk X post after October 13 close (TrendForce/Yahoo relays)
confidence_language: confirmed (TrendForce primary; Katti via secondary relays of WSJ)
dispatch_note: Consolidates research-intake VULCAN watch items (Musk/Micron x3, TrendForce, AMD TAM) and a Will bookmark (OpenAI computing chief). Verified by a RULE 9 helper. Counterweight to SIG-W-20261014-018: projected capex keeps rising while the financing/equity side sold off.
body: 1) TrendForce (primary, October 14): capex of the nine largest cloud providers (Google, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle, ByteDance, Tencent, Alibaba, Baidu) now $957B in 2026 (+106% y/y) and >$1.5T in 2027 (+60%), up from >$886.7B and ~$1.3T in its August 3 release. AI server revenue ~$920B in 2027 (>+90%) on only ~+36% unit shipments; total server revenue passes $1T. Caveat that travels: TrendForce attributes much of the growth to component price increases amid shortages (especially memory) and supplier prepayments pulling cash forward, so the capex rise is largely price and timing, not volume; all figures are projections. 2) AMD (Open Compute Project keynote, October 12 Pacific): Lisa Su put the 2030 CPU TAM at 'over $200 billion' (~50% CAGR), raised 'three times in the last nine months' (prior ~$60B November 2025 and >$120B May 2026, secondary sources), and the data-centre AI accelerator TAM 'approaching $1.5 trillion by 2030'; unclear whether the CPU figure is server-only; a TAM is not AMD revenue. AMD closed -5.73% on October 14. 3) Micron: Musk posted after the October 13 close that Micron 'has been reasonable regarding future memory prices, while others have been extortionate' (rivals unnamed, read as Samsung/SK hynix). MU fell anyway: -3.62% October 13 and -4.10% October 14 to $914.13, its fifth straight decline and -16.0% from the October 7 close. The circulating '-3.2%' matches neither close. 4) OpenAI: computing-capacity head Sachin Katti (ex-Intel CTO, about one year in role) is leaving, last day November 15, staying as an adviser (WSJ, via secondary relays; WSJ not read). A named successor (Uday Ruddarraju) appears in one secondary source only, unverified. Earlier exit: data-centre head Chris Malone, August 2026.

title: 'Anthropic below $2 trillion' is the price of a thin synthetic perpetual on Hyperliquid, not a valuation; the last primary round was $965B
origin: Hyperliquid public info API, pulled 00:24Z October 15
Orrick (Anthropic counsel) Series H announcement, May 29 2026
confidence_language: venue and prices confirmed; valuation conversion is a convention
dispatch_note: Will bookmark (unusual_whales: 'Anthropic down >10% in a month, >$200B wiped from implied valuation, pre-IPO perpetual below $2T on Liquid'). RULE 9 helper verdict CORRECTED-FRAMING; RED on info. Distinct from the Ornn index item corrected in SIG-W-20261014-010.
body: The price is real but the instrument is not equity. 'Liquid' is a non-custodial trading app; the market io:ANTH is a synthetic perpetual run by EntropyIO on Hyperliquid (builder-deployed HIP-3 market), up to 6x leverage, giving price exposure with no claim on Anthropic shares. At 00:24Z October 15: mark $1,934.3 (-4.8% over 24h), 24h volume $23.7M, open interest about $39.7M. Daily closes fell from $2,204.9 (September 14) to $1,940.9 (October 14), -12.0%. Turning that into '$1.93T, about $270B lower' requires an assumed ~1B share count (a venue convention, not a company figure). Other venues quote $1,619 and $2,000 with zero open interest. The last primary round was Series H, $65B at $965B post-money (May 29, 2026), so this contract prices Anthropic at roughly 2x the round. Do not cite it as Anthropic's valuation. Unverified: Liquid's own attribution of the decline to de-risking before a reported Q3 disclosure and a reported November IPO roadshow.
